name: Puget Sound
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_features: Elevated green tight to a bank; drop-off left to short grass ~15 ft below; small bunker off the back; approach favours the right side.
notes: Large landform and bunker up the right; partially blind second over a crest (S7, S17). Current card: par 4. 2015 U.S. Open: par 4 (496 yd) in R1, R3, R4 and par 5 (598 yd) in R2, swapping with No. 18 to keep par 70 (S18, S32). Older daily card listed it as a 559-yd par 5 from Navy (S4); 2010 U.S. Amateur 501/542 yd, par 4/5 (S20).

name: Foxy
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Falls right-to-left off the right side toward the big left bunker
green_features: Split by a large ridge; large bunker left, small bunker right; open entrance from the right.
notes: Knob in the landing area (S5). Name references the 14th at Royal Dornoch (S22; that page's body text spells it 'Roxy'). 2015 U.S. Open: 399 yd (S19).

name: Blown Out
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Redan-style, slopes front-right to back-left
green_features: Kidney-shaped with a small ridge; deep bunker and deep fescue left; swale behind collects long shots; large kick slope on the right.
notes: 2015 U.S. Open: 163-198 yd depending on the day (S5, S18).

name: Hazard's Ascent
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_features: Large and heavily contoured; sand on three sides (front bunker running down the right, three blowout bunkers in the banks behind); natural backstop for long shots.
notes: Immense bunker complex along the right off the tee (S5, S7). Current card: par 5. Played as a par 4 (495 yd) at the 2015 U.S. Open (S5, S19); par 5 (568 yd) at the 2010 U.S. Amateur (S20).

name: Free Fall
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Severely back-to-front
green_features: Deep pot bunker fronting the green; low chipping area behind.
notes: Fairway slopes left and narrows just past 300 yd; massive bunker complexes on both sides; semi-blind approach from the left (S5, S6, S7). A former alternate second green was removed before 2015 (S5). 2015 U.S. Open: 488 yd (S19).

name: Deception Point
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Back-to-front
green_features: Long, narrow green perched between two bunkers and framed by dunes and long bunkers.
notes: Partially blind tee shot; plays as a dogleg right or short and straight depending on tee (S6, S7). Lengthened ~100 yd for 2015, playing 495 yd (S5, S19).

name: Humpback
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_features: Elevated, multi-tiered: significant false front and a perpendicular ridge creating three shelves; two hummocks short-left block the view from the left.
notes: Bends right around a large bunker/waste complex on the right; aim left off the tee (S5, S24). Stroke index 1; operator calls it the hardest hole for all levels (S16). 2015 U.S. Open: 508 yd (S19).

name: High Road Low Road
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_features: Long and narrow with several ridges; contours left and back; area right of the green is blind.
notes: In 2015 the only hole without a bunker (S5). Hillside left, steep drop right; fairway slopes left-to-right (S5, S7). 2015 U.S. Open: 614 yd, the longest hole (S5, S19).

name: Olympus
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Left-to-right
green_features: Oversized, one of the largest on the course; contours funnel balls toward the hole; large bunker short-right.
notes: Tee is the course's high point. 2015 U.S. Open used both tees (224 upper / 217 lower, about a 90-degree change in angle); round yardages 203, 237, 225, 203 (S36, S34, S18).

name: High Dunes
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Slopes away from the dunes
green_features: Relatively flat, tucked between dunes; deep bunkers front-right and back-left.
notes: Landing area narrows between dunes and sand; diagonal approach (S5, S6). 2015 U.S. Open: 436/468 yd (S18).

name: Shadows
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Right-to-left, falls down to the left
green_features: Slightly elevated; ridge bisects it lengthwise; misplayed shots can roll ~40 yd away. Approach from the right.
notes: Dogleg left with a hillock/mound in the middle of the fairway (carry ~300 yd); hillside right, drop-off left (S5, S33, S17). 2015 U.S. Open: 500/537 yd (S18).

name: The Narrows
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Severely back-to-front
green_features: Largest green on the course (~12,700 sq ft, S13), set in a punchbowl; long and skinny between two large mounds with distinct quadrants. Depth published only as 'over 60 yards' (S17), so 60 is a lower bound.
notes: Drivable par 4 and the narrowest hole; large blowout bunker short-left of the green (S5, S7). 2015 U.S. Open round yardages: 317, 284, 311, 270 (S18).

name: Eagle Eye
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Falls away on the right
green_features: Deep bunker in front; knob left of the green.
notes: Dogleg right; widest fairway on the course (~115 yd) with a centreline bunker (S5, S7, S17). Current card: par 5 (519 yd from Black, confirmed by S17). Played as a 534-yd par 4 at the 2015 U.S. Open (S19); older Navy card listed it as a 485-yd par 4 (S4).

name: Cape Fear
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Tilts toward the front, then the back slopes away
green_features: Large, with a pronounced central ridge; back funnels balls away; collection area right; mound short-right.
notes: Downhill tee shot over the course's largest waste area/bunker complex on the left, plus a centreline fairway bunker (S5, S9, S17). 546 yd in 2015 was the longest par 4 in U.S. Open history (S9); 2015 tees 521/546 (S18).

name: Lone Fir
penalty_areas: No water hazard on the course per the designer (S12). Puget Sound lies behind the green beyond the BNSF railway (S27); no source documents it as a marked penalty area.
green_slope: Left-to-right
green_features: Two-section green; the front repels poorly struck shots; well defended by waste bunkers.
notes: The course's only tree (a Douglas fir) stands behind the green; fully exposed to wind off Puget Sound (S5, S7). 2015 U.S. Open: 123-246 yd range, round yardages 169, 144, 252, 158 (S18).

name: Beached
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Slopes sharply left-to-right
green_features: Smallest green on the course: tabletop, pear-shaped, about twice as wide at the front as the back; back tongue narrows to ~9 yd wide. ~50 yd deep (S17).
notes: Short par 4, drivable from forward tees. Railroad and Puget Sound to the right; a long bunker/waste area runs the entire right side; fairway narrows just short of 300 yd (S5, S7, S25). 2015 U.S. Open: 423 yd (S19). Name conflict: S27 (2026) calls No. 16 'Derailed'; most sources give 'Beached' (S6, S7, S4).

name: Derailed
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Middle tier slopes right-to-left
green_features: Split into two halves; right pins very hard to reach; bunker short-left; a long miss leaves a hard up-and-down.
notes: Long carry over a waste bunker and native area from the lower tee; the BNSF rail line runs the length of the right side, with Puget Sound beyond (S26, S35, S17, S6). 2015 U.S. Open: 172-218 yd (S18).

name: Tahoma
penalty_areas: No water on the hole; the course has no water hazards (designer, S12). No marked penalty area documented.
green_slope: Multiple levels, strongly contoured
green_features: One of the largest and most severe greens. USGA describes four sections with the back-right hardest (S15); GOLF.com describes three tiers (S11). Bowl-shaped (S17).
notes: Deep (~10 ft) cross bunker mid-fairway about 120 yd from the green; large bunker complex right (S5, S17, S6). Current card: par 5. 2015 U.S. Open: par 5 (604 yd) in R1, R3, R4 and par 4 (525 yd) in R2 (S18, S32).

name: Burn
penalty_areas: Swilcan Burn runs down the right of the fairway and across the front of the green. Its marking colour is not confirmed.
green_slope: Front half fairly flat; slopes and ripples at the back, with a back-left upper shelf.
green_features: Single green, no bunkers; fronted by the Swilcan Burn.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 12. Shared fairway with the 18th, 129 yards wide (7.2 acres). Open yardages: 2015 375, 2022 375, 2027 (proposed) 375; 2024 AIG Women's Open 375.

name: Dyke
green_slope: Series of ridges into the left half, with a 4-5 ft drop from high to low; diagonal ridge at the front.
green_features: Double green shared with the 16th; two bunkers to the right of the green.
notes: Women's par 5, women's SI 14. Gorse right; Cheape's bunker left, about 300 yds from the championship tee (2015). 2027: right-side fairway bunkers moved further down the hole. Open yardages: 2015 452, 2022 452, 2027 (proposed) 452; 2024 AIG Women's Open 400.

name: Cartgate (Out)
green_slope: Vast, with subtle undulations and a counter-break. The back-right quarter is a lower tier, and a small ridge at the front can kick balls.
green_features: Double green shared with the 15th; the Cartgate bunker cuts into the front-left.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 8. Bunker on the left of the fairway. Open yardages: 2015 398, 2022 398, 2027 (proposed) 398; 2024 AIG Women's Open 366.

name: Ginger Beer
green_slope: Slopes away to the right, falling sharply from the left over successive shoulders; the rear shelf is hard to reach.
green_features: Double green shared with the 14th; deep bunker left, hidden bunker right; Ginger Beer pot bunker behind.
notes: Women's par 5, women's SI 6. Narrow fairway with mounds left and gorse right. Open yardages: 2015 480, 2022 480, 2027 (proposed) 480; 2024 AIG Women's Open 413.

name: Hole O'Cross (Out)
green_slope: Steep drop-off along the front left; deep swale in front.
green_features: Double green shared with the 13th and the largest on the course; 37,846 sq ft is the whole double green. Depth is given as 92 yd (Golf Channel), 99 yd (Fried Egg) and about 100 yd (R&A).
notes: Women's par 5, women's SI 2. Seven bunkers right of the fairway; the Spectacles (two deep pots) sit about 50-60 yds short of the green. 2027: new championship tee. Open yardages: 2015 570, 2022 570, 2027 (proposed) 605; 2024 AIG Women's Open 525.

name: Heathery (Out)
green_slope: Relatively flat, with a 3-4 ft false front that falls away and a hidden swale in front.
green_features: Double green shared with the 12th; 104 yd is the width of the whole double green. No greenside bunkers.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 10. Blind tee shot; Coffin bunkers and hidden bunkers. 2027: new championship tee, road realignment and new left fairway bunker. Open yardages: 2015 414, 2022 414, 2027 (proposed) 431; 2024 AIG Women's Open 370.

name: High (Out)
green_slope: Winds and slopes from left to right; quieter ripples at the back.
green_features: Double green shared with the 11th; 112 yd is the width of the whole double green. Shell bunker guards the approach.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 4. The course's only true dogleg. Huge Shell bunker about 310 yds from the championship tee. 2027: new championship tee. Open yardages: 2015 371, 2022 371, 2027 (proposed) 393; 2024 AIG Women's Open 361.

name: Short
green_slope: Relatively flat; the front feeds away from the tee and the rear climbs to a shallow ridge with a steep drop behind. Tricky to read.
green_features: Double green shared with the 10th; 36,063 sq ft is the whole double green. Short Hole pot bunker guards the front left.
notes: Women's par 3, women's SI 18. Open yardages: 2015 174, 2022 187, 2027 (proposed) 187; 2024 AIG Women's Open 173.

name: End
green_slope: Relatively flat, tilting slightly from back left to front.
green_features: Single green; two bunkers in front, gorse close to the left. Few visual cues for judging distance.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 16. Fairway bunkers right at about 260 and 290 yds (championship tee); gorse left. 2027: approach bunkers widened slightly. Open yardages: 2015 352, 2022 352, 2027 (proposed) 352; 2024 AIG Women's Open 349.

name: Bobby Jones
green_slope: Slopes front to back, falling away from a raised front, with subtle undulations.
green_features: Double green shared with the 8th; 36,063 sq ft is the whole double green.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 13. Narrow, undulating fairway; two small bunkers right at about 290 yds. 2027: new championship tee and new left fairway bunker. Open yardages: 2015 386, 2022 386, 2027 (proposed) 415; 2024 AIG Women's Open 341.

name: High (In)
penalty_areas: The Eden estuary sits just behind the green, below a steep drop-off. Whether it is a penalty area or out of bounds is not confirmed.
green_slope: Slopes severely from back to front, with a large false front; very steep run-off over the back.
green_features: Double green shared with the 7th (112 yd is the whole green). R&A calls it probably the second-shallowest green after the 17th. Hill bunker front-left and Strath pot bunker front.
notes: Women's par 3, women's SI 17. The original 'Eden' hole, fully exposed to wind off the estuary. 2027: championship tee extended. Open yardages: 2015 174, 2022 174, 2027 (proposed) 195; 2024 AIG Women's Open 165.

name: Heathery (In)
green_slope: Two tiers; the top tier is only 12 paces deep (about 18 on the right). A hump on the right and hollows pinch the sides.
green_features: Double green shared with the 6th (104 yd is the whole green); prominent central pot bunker.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 3. Short par 4 that long hitters can drive; several bunkers in the centre of the fairway are hidden from the tee, with gorse left and right. 2027: tees adjusted and area before the approach bunker reshaped. Open yardages: 2015 348, 2022 351, 2027 (proposed) 349; 2024 AIG Women's Open 351.

name: Hole O'Cross (In)
green_slope: Shallow hollow to the left; pockets above a steep drop-off.
green_features: Double green shared with the 5th; 37,846 sq ft is the whole double green. A narrow entrance between the Lion's Mouth bunker and a pot; swale and bunker to the right.
notes: Women's par 5, women's SI 11. Coffin bunkers just under 300 yds from the championship tee; fairway ends around 300 yds. Open yardages: 2015 465, 2022 465, 2027 (proposed) 465; 2024 AIG Women's Open 430.

name: Long
green_slope: Steep front face, then falls away to the back and left; bulky dune shoulder at the front right.
green_features: Double green shared with the 4th; sand surrounds the green.
notes: Women's par 5, women's SI 1. Beardies bunkers left off the tee; the second shot must avoid Hell bunker (about 10 ft deep; its area is given as 300 sq m, 300 sq yd or 300 sq ft depending on the source). 2027: tee realigned, the only 2027 tee change that affects everyday golfers. Open yardages: 2015 614, 2022 614, 2027 (proposed) 614; 2024 AIG Women's Open 577.

name: Cartgate (In)
green_slope: Deceptively deep and hard to read; humps and bumps in front, then a slope that is steeper at first and flattens out.
green_features: Double green shared with the 3rd; pot bunker front left.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 5. Fairway narrows around 300 yds; Sutherland bunker mid-fairway, with pot bunkers further up. Open yardages: 2015 455, 2022 455, 2027 (proposed) 455; 2024 AIG Women's Open 415.

name: Corner of the Dyke
green_slope: Rises sharply at the front.
green_features: Double green shared with the 2nd; bunkers in front and behind. The front-right pin is about eight paces from the boundary fence.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 9. Principal's Nose (three bunkers) in the centre of the fairway; risk/reward tee shot between them and the OB. 2027: championship tee extended, fairway restored left of the Principal's Nose and two bunkers added. Open yardages: 2015 418, 2022 418, 2027 (proposed) 428; 2024 AIG Women's Open 380.

name: Road
green_slope: Set at about 45 degrees between the Road Hole bunker and the road, banked about 2-3%; the right half is the preferred side.
green_features: Single green and the smallest on the course (7,078 sq ft). The R&A calls it the shallowest green; 10 yd is its shallowest point. Road Hole bunker front-left; path, road and wall behind.
notes: Women's par 5, women's SI 7. Blind drive over the hotel corner; from the championship tee the carry over the replica shed is about 260 yds (2015). For the 2010 Open the championship tee moved back about 40 yds. 2027: ridge left of the Road Hole bunker lowered; the bunker's size and shape are unchanged. Open yardages: 2015 495, 2022 495, 2027 (proposed) 495; 2024 AIG Women's Open 439.

name: Tom Morris
penalty_areas: Swilcan Burn crosses the shared fairway about 30-40 yds in front of the tee (Swilcan Bridge). Its marking colour is not confirmed.
green_slope: Large and undulating, with a back-right slant across the green; the rear-left section is flatter than it looks.
green_features: Single green, the largest single green (15,570 sq ft). Valley of Sin short left; boundary fence just behind.
notes: Women's par 4, women's SI 15. Drivable for long hitters. The Blue tee (366) is listed longer than the Black (354); the 2019 card showed the same pattern (yellow 361 vs white 357). Open yardages: 2015 356, 2022 356, 2027 (proposed) 356; 2024 AIG Women's Open 354.

green_slope: Tilts back-to-front toward the ocean.
green_features: Elevated; bunkers on both sides.
notes: Dogleg right; tee shot is effectively a layup toward the corner fairway bunker, leaving ~150 yds in; trees block cutting the corner right (S3, S8). Women's handicap 10 (S1). Tournament yardages: 381 (AT&T 2026), 380 (U.S. Open 2019), 344 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: A barranca/ditch crosses the hole about 100 yards short of the green and guards the layup area (marking colour not confirmed).
green_features: Narrow green with a bunker along each side; the right bunker is the less forgiving.
notes: Par 5 for resort play, the AT&T Pro-Am and the 2023 U.S. Women's Open, but played as a 516-yd par 4 at the U.S. Open since 2000 (course par 71). Back tee moved back 14 yds before 2019 (502 to 516) (S12, S17, S31). Fairway ends ~100 yds short of the green with a hidden cross bunker (S3). Women's handicap 6 (S1). Tournament yardages: 516 (AT&T 2026), 516 (U.S. Open 2019, par 4), 507 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Ravine crossed off the tee (marking not confirmed).
green_slope: Runs toward the ocean (right-to-left per S44).
green_features: Slightly elevated with deep bunkers on both sides; Hale Irwin called it the hardest green to read in the world.
notes: Severe dogleg left; long hitters can carry the trees on the left; second shot usually into the Pacific breeze (S8). Women's handicap 12 (S1). Tournament yardages: 404 (AT&T 2026), 404 (U.S. Open 2019), 381 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Pacific Ocean (Stillwater Cove) and bluff to the right of the fairway and green; first of the seaside holes (ocean in play from No. 4 through No. 10).
green_slope: Steeply pitched back-to-front; shots above the hole leave a hard putt.
green_features: Surrounded by bunkers; nine bunkers on the hole; 26 paces deep (S10).
notes: Short par 4; tee shot must clear a cross bunker; driver can run just short of the green but brings the left bunker and the ocean right into play. Only par 4 to play under par at the 2019 U.S. Open (S3, S8). Fairway shaved to run off toward the coastline in U.S. Open setup (S17). Women's handicap 14 (S1). Tournament yardages: 331 (AT&T 2026), 331 (U.S. Open 2019), 307 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Hole sits on the Pacific bluffs above Stillwater Cove (ocean to the right).
green_slope: Slopes front-left to back-right; the only green on the course not pitched back-to-front.
green_features: Shallow and wind-exposed; small bunkers in front, larger bunker back-left that cuts into the putting surface more than it appears.
notes: Jack Nicklaus-designed hole opened 1998 (S3, S10). Safe play is left-centre (S8). Women's handicap 16 (S1). Tournament yardages: 195 (AT&T 2026), 195 (U.S. Open 2019), 186 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Cliff and Stillwater Cove (Pacific Ocean) along the right; rough on the right was mowed short so wayward drives can run over the cliff. A rough buffer was added on the right before the 2023 U.S. Women's Open (S28).
green_features: Hilltop green bunkered on both sides; one of five original 1919 greens (S11).
notes: Penal bunkers down the left off the tee; tee re-angled toward Stillwater Cove in 2016 (S12, S28). New back tee for the 2026 AT&T Pro-Am made it 540 yds (523 in 2025, +17) (S4, S5, S27). Women's handicap 4 (S1). Tournament yardages: 540 (AT&T 2026), 523 (U.S. Open 2019), 493 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Pacific Ocean and rocks to the right, behind and left of the green (surrounded on three sides).
green_slope: Everything breaks toward the ocean.
green_features: Tiny green ringed by six bunkers (S8); 'just over 20 yards deep' (S25). Rebuilt 1992 (S16).
notes: Shortest hole on the PGA TOUR; played 92 yds in the final round of the 2010 U.S. Open (S16, S24). Women's handicap 18 (S1). Tournament yardages: 106 (AT&T 2026), 109 (U.S. Open 2019), 107 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Pacific Ocean chasm/cliff along the right and in front of the green (approach carries ~180+ yds over it, S35). Red penalty-area line on the cliff side of the fairway was moved to 6 ft from the edge in 2022, with longer rough between fairway and bluff.
green_slope: Steeply back-to-front with a false front; balls that fail to crest it roll back to the approach; breaks toward the Pacific.
green_features: 2022 restoration reclaimed 400 sq ft on an original 2,700 sq ft green (~3,100; Golf Digest says 'just over 3,000'); usable hole-location area more than doubled. Bunker short; two bunkers behind. 21-22 paces deep (S9, S10).
notes: Aiming rock guides the tee shot from the lower tees; usually a 3-wood off the tee. Jordan Spieth played from the cliff edge in 2022, prompting the penalty-line change (S3, S8, S22, S23). Fairway narrowed for the 2023 U.S. Women's Open (S31). Women's handicap 2 (S1). Tournament yardages: 428 (AT&T 2026), 428 (U.S. Open 2019), 394 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Pacific Ocean / Carmel Beach the full length of the right side, with a sheer drop to the beach right of the green.
green_features: One of the two smallest greens (S9); 23 paces deep (S9). Restored 2013, reclaiming ~600 sq ft on the left (Pebble Beach later said ~700) and softening the back-to-front slope. Gully with two bunkers short-left.
notes: Hardest hole at the 2019 U.S. Open (S3). New 21-yd back tee for 2019 (526 yds) (S12). Fairway shaved toward the coastline for U.S. Open setup (S17). Women's handicap 8 (S1). Tournament yardages: 504 (AT&T 2026), 526 (U.S. Open 2019), 432 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Pacific Ocean / Carmel Beach the full length of the right side; steep drop to the beach right of the green; penalty area near the front and middle-right of the restored green.
green_slope: Slopes severely toward the ocean (right).
green_features: On a bluff; bunkers catch misses long and left. Original 1919 green (S11), restored and expanded in 2025 after shrinking to a few hundred sq ft of pinnable surface (S30).
notes: Widest fairway on the course (S3); three fairway bunkers punish left misses (S18). A cliff-edge tee between the 9th green and the ocean was used in Feb 2021 (356 yds) (S29). Women's handicap 7 (S1). Tournament yardages: 446 (AT&T 2026), 495 (U.S. Open 2019), 428 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

green_slope: Severe back-to-front; strongest back-to-front slope on the course. Stay below the hole.
green_features: Among the smallest greens; bunkers back and right. Measured 2,200 sq ft in 2019 (S20) but restored in 2021 to regain lost area (S32); current size not published.
notes: Turns inland away from the ocean; fairway metal typical off the tee (S8). Women's handicap 9 (S1). Tournament yardages: 390 (AT&T 2026), 390 (U.S. Open 2019), 367 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

green_slope: Shots finding the throat kick left toward the ocean (S3).
green_features: Wide but shallow; a large bunker guards most of the entrance. Original 1919 green (S11).
notes: Hard to hold when firm; best miss short-right except for front-left pins; trees on the right hide the wind (S8). Women's handicap 13 (S1). Tournament yardages: 202 (AT&T 2026), 202 (U.S. Open 2019), 173 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

green_slope: Pitches hard right-to-left toward the ocean (tamed slightly in 2017).
green_features: Rebuilt 2017 adding ~400 sq ft on the right (Pebble Beach's 2019 summary says 300); restored left bunker sits ~6 ft below the surface.
notes: Bunker complex left of the fairway, three small bunkers right (S8). Women's handicap 11 (S1). Tournament yardages: 445 (AT&T 2026), 445 (U.S. Open 2019), 389 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

green_slope: Back-right slope softened in 2016 for new pin positions (S12).
green_features: Elevated, walled off by a deep front bunker and a large false front that climbs halfway into the green; left side shaved. Expanded in 2016 from ~3,000 sq ft (Pebble Beach: 'nearly 4,000' after; +800 sq ft). 25 paces deep (S10).
notes: Dogleg right around trees with two large bunkers at the corner; among the hardest par 5s in championship golf; played over par at the 2019 U.S. Open (S3, S8). Women's handicap 1 (S1). Tournament yardages: 580 (AT&T 2026), 580 (U.S. Open 2019), 545 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Tee shot crosses a barranca (marking not confirmed).
green_slope: Slopes severely left, toward the unseen ocean.
green_features: Well guarded; bunkers left.
notes: Lay up short of the mid-fairway pot bunker to leave under 125 yds (S3). Women's handicap 15 (S1). Tournament yardages: 397 (AT&T 2026), 397 (U.S. Open 2019), 374 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Ravine/barranca in front of the green on the approach (marking not confirmed).
green_slope: Pitches sharply right-to-left.
green_features: Deep bunker short, small bunker long, trees left. Original 1919 green (S11).
notes: Tee shot must clear or avoid a mid-fairway island bunker, leaving ~150 yds in (S3, S8). Women's handicap 5 (S1). Tournament yardages: 403 (AT&T 2026), 403 (U.S. Open 2019), 376 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Pacific Ocean in play to the left.
green_features: Hourglass/figure-eight shape; can play 15 yds longer or shorter depending on the pin (S3) with a massive front bunker and smaller bunkers long. Largest green on the course; restored 2015 from ~3,600 to ~5,000 sq ft per Pebble Beach (GolfPass gives 5,123). Left half 16 paces deep (S10).
notes: Usually plays into the Pacific wind; traditional Sunday U.S. Open pin is back-left (S3, S8). Women's handicap 17 (S1). Tournament yardages: 178 (AT&T 2026), 208 (U.S. Open 2019), 175 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

penalty_areas: Pacific Ocean (Stillwater Cove) the full length of the left side behind a sea wall; drive carries rocks along the shore.
green_features: Deep bunker right; towering pines left push play toward the ocean. Original 1919 green (S11).
notes: Curves slightly right-to-left along the coast; tree in the fairway: drive left of it to reach in two, or right of it and lay up (S3, S26). Landing area ~25 yds wide between tree and ocean in U.S. Open setup (S17). Women's handicap 3 (S1). Tournament yardages: 543 (AT&T 2026), 543 (U.S. Open 2019), 527 (U.S. Women's Open 2023).

green_slope: Large hump in the left-middle of the green; approach is best played from the right side.
notes: Women's handicap 9. Favor the left side off the tee (S1). USGA championship yardage 398 (2020 U.S. Amateur, S7) and 400 (2022 U.S. Junior Amateur, S8). Stymie (S4) lists 399 from the Black tee and 341 from Gold, against 386 and 332 on the other scorecards.

green_slope: Severely undulating. A blog source describes a back tier, a slope on the left and a backboard on the right that feeds balls back.
green_features: Collection area right of the green is the common miss (S14). The blog mentions a pot bunker short (S21).
notes: Women's handicap 13. The prevailing wind is into the player and from the left, pushing shots short or right (S1, S14). The Royal Blue yardage conflicts between sources: 76 (S5, S6; sums to the rated 3,945 total), 117 (S2 scorecard) and 130 (S4). The Orange yardage is 130 in S3/S4/S5/S6 but 117 in the S2 scorecard.

Women's handicap 1. Described as the first real birdie chance; the landing area for the second shot can be blind from the fairway (S1). The Orange yardage is 370 in S3/S5/S6 but 351 in the S2 scorecard.

penalty_areas: Pacific Ocean and bluff directly beyond the green; long shots are at risk.
green_features: An 'infinity' green set on the bluffs with breakers behind (Kidd, S10). Deep bunkers guard the front-left.
notes: Women's handicap 17. Dogleg right toward the ocean (S10, S16). Aim the tee shot at the bunker straight ahead; a low shot up the right is often best (S1).

penalty_areas: The ocean runs along the left; the sea is heard but largely hidden by dunes from the fairway. Gorse originally encroached from the right. Native grass islands sit in the fairway (now trampled, per Kidd).
green_features: Framed by mounds on both sides.
notes: Women's handicap 7. Split fairway; drive into the right half (S1). Plays straight into the prevailing summer (north) wind and can be a three-shot hole (S1, S10). USGA championship tee 472 (2020, S7) and 473 (2022, S8) is longer than the official 445. Stymie (S4) shows a 473-yard tee as par 5, which conflicts with every other source (par 4).

penalty_areas: Seaside par 3 (ocean adjacent; which side is not specified).
green_features: Deep bunker left; a miss right leaves a manageable chip.
notes: Women's handicap 15. Plays much longer than the yardage because of the wind (S1).

green_slope: Effectively three-tiered; the pin position matters greatly.
notes: Women's handicap 5. The fairway is wider than it looks; favor the left, over an outcrop of beach grass (S1).

green_slope: Hump at the front-left can feed balls toward the center.
green_features: A narrow front opening makes the green look smaller than it is.
notes: Women's handicap 11. Cross bunkers off the tee; the carry yardage can be deceptive (S1).

Women's handicap 3. Pot bunkers sit in the center of the landing zone. The left offers a wider fairway but a longer approach; going right of the bunkers with the usual wind help can make it reachable in two (S1). Stymie (S4) lists a 605-yard tournament tee.

green_features: Shallow green.
notes: Women's handicap 10. A drive right gives the shortest approach; the left gives the best angle. The second shot is blind (S1).

green_slope: Slopes away from the player.
green_features: Bunker right of the green.
notes: Women's handicap 12. Plays long, straight into the summer wind (S1, S10). USGA championship tee is 469 (2020, S7; 2022, S8), against the official 452.

penalty_areas: Green sits along the sea (side not specified).
green_features: Shallow, firm green. A sod-faced bunker guards short shots, native fescue rises behind, and the open approach is front-right.
notes: Women's handicap 18. Club selection is critical (S1). USGA used 199 for the 2020 and 2022 championships (S7, S8), against 238 on the official card.

penalty_areas: The course's only internal water hazard, in play on drives to the left.
green_features: Deep collection area short of the green.
notes: Women's handicap 6. Reachable downwind; terrain on the right can leave awkward lies (S1). The Tournament and Black tees are both 553.

green_features: Shallow, elongated green behind a distant dune. Kidd enlarged a small pot bunker at the green's right corner into a large sand area (S11).
notes: Women's handicap 14. Dogleg right; use a fairway bunker as the aiming line, and drives left give a better angle (S1). Three bunkers pinch the wide fairway (S10). Nearly drivable in calm air by cutting the corner (S11).

penalty_areas: Green sits along the sea (side not specified).
green_slope: A bank on the left feeds shots toward the center.
green_features: Narrow, exposed green. The deepest bunker on the course is front-right: a 2013 review put it about 20-30 ft below the putting surface (S15), and Kidd reworked it smaller and shallower in 2019 (S10).
notes: Women's handicap 16. Favor the left (S1, S11). Usually plays into the wind; in a 20-30 mph headwind a bunted driver may be needed (S11).

penalty_areas: Cliff and Pacific to the right and behind the green; pin flags sit feet from a near-vertical drop of about 100 ft to the beach. Gorse right of the green is closer than it looks. A sandy waste area lies in front of and below the green (S21).
green_slope: Falls away at the front, left and back; the cliff is on the right (blog source, S21).
green_features: Green on the cliff edge (rebuilt/'revised' per Kidd, S12). Avoid attacking right-side pins (S1).
notes: Women's handicap 4. A driveable par 4 downwind. Kidd suggests a 3-wood aimed long-left toward the 17th tee and warns that the slightest miss right loses the hole (S10, S11). Stymie (S4) lists a 412-yard tournament tee; the official card shows 363 for both Tournament and Black.

penalty_areas: The drive carries part of the coastline (S20). A blog source describes a chasm/ravine down the right side to the green (S21).
green_features: Largest green on the property at about 80 yards front to back (Kidd); the official guide calls it the deepest green on the course (S1).
notes: Women's handicap 8. A drive down the left gives the best angle (S1); the landing area narrows the farther you hit it (S10), and a north wind pushes the ball right (S11). Bend Bulletin (S20) called it 420 yards in 2020; official 405; USGA used 405 (2020) and 389 (2022).

penalty_areas: A hazard plus bunkers on the right side of the dogleg (type and marking not specified).
green_features: From the right side the green is hidden, and two bunkers block run-up approaches (S11).
notes: Women's handicap 2. Dogleg right. Drive left, aiming at the top of the golf shop (S11); the second shot is blind, so use the right edge of the clubhouse as a reference (S1). The lodge sits behind the green (S15).

penalty_areas: Water (penalty area) along the right side of the landing area.
green_features: Long, narrow green; large bunkers front and left, grass bunkers front-right, right and behind.
notes: Slight dogleg right with a narrow landing area; trees left, long fairway bunker right (S4). Mounds (moguls) past the right fairway bunker were strengthened and three pot bunkers added in 2016 (S18). TPC's yardage guide calls it a mirror image of No. 10 (S2). Women's handicap 11 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water right off the tee, plus a small pond right that guards the approach from about 175 yards out.
green_features: Deep sand and grass bunkers around the green; spectator mounds.
notes: Short, reachable par 5; trees both sides (S4). New tournament tee in 2025 took it from 532 to 555 yards (S13). Women's handicap 1 (S1).

penalty_areas: No water in the official hole description.
green_slope: Two tiers, sloping back to front.
green_features: Bunker front, grass bunkers right, large bunker left and back-left.
notes: Women's handicap 17 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water and a deep bunker right of the fairway; water across the front and left of the green.
green_slope: Two tiers, very undulating.
green_features: Shallowest green on the course (25-yd depth); small deep bunkers right and behind; spectator mounds behind.
notes: Short par 4 that demands accuracy (S4). Women's handicap 5 (S1).

penalty_areas: No water in the official hole description.
green_slope: Rolling.
green_features: Deep, narrow green; grass and sand bunkers, a waste area and palms around it.
notes: Dogleg right with a generous landing area; long bunker down the right (S4). Women's handicap 7 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water down the left (lake enlarged in the 2016 renovation, when mounding between Nos. 6 and 7 was replaced by water).
green_slope: Two tiers; slopes right to left and back to front.
green_features: Bunkers and palms around the green.
notes: Target-style hole; dense trees right, two fairway bunkers left (S4). New tournament tee in 2025 (393 to 413 yards) and the overhanging tree near the tee was restored (S13, S5). Women's handicap 13 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water and a large fairway bunker along most of the left side (lake added in the 2016 renovation).
green_slope: Falls away sharply off the back.
green_features: Bunkers front and left.
notes: Long, slight dogleg right; thick trees right. The tee was moved about 5 yards right when the lake was enlarged (S4). Women's handicap 9 (S1).

penalty_areas: No water in the official hole description.
green_slope: Sloping.
green_features: Deep, narrow green ringed by sand and grass bunkers; open at the front for running shots.
notes: Longest par 3 on the course (S1, S4). Women's handicap 15 (S1).

penalty_areas: Large lake right of the fairway; it is the same lake that runs along the left of No. 18.
green_slope: Slopes steeply from the front to the back right.
green_features: Very thin green; banked bunkers left and behind; spectator mound behind.
notes: Longest hole (S1). Woods left affect the second shot (S4). A tee added in the 2016 renovation gives the option of playing it about 20 yards longer (S18). Women's handicap 3 (S1).

penalty_areas: No water in the official hole description.
green_slope: Falls away from the player.
green_features: Looks large from the fairway but is narrow; two bunkers front-right, grass bunkers left.
notes: Dogleg left; large bunker left, dense trees right (S4). TPC's yardage guide calls it a mirror image of No. 1 (S2). Women's handicap 10 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water splits the fairway in the second-shot area and continues around the back of the green.
green_features: Bunker across the front; closely mown run-off on the left.
notes: Dense trees and a very large bunker beside the driving area (S4). New tee in 2025 (558 to 573 yards); the left fairway bunker was moved back (S13). Women's handicap 2 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water left of the green and alongside the long bunker that runs up the left of the fairway.
green_slope: Several tiers; slopes sharply toward the water on the left.
green_features: Pot bunkers and rough ground right; trees beyond the green for drives that run through.
notes: Rebuilt in 2016 as a drivable dogleg-left par 4 (about 302 yards from a forward tee option) (S7, S4). Women's handicap 14 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water along the entire left side.
green_slope: Three tiers; the left side drops steeply toward the water.
green_features: Two small, deep bunkers.
notes: Women's handicap 18 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water and a fairway bunker left of the driving area.
green_slope: Severe undulations and long slopes.
green_features: Very large green; bunkers front-left, right and behind.
notes: Hardest hole at the 2025 PLAYERS (difficulty rank 1) (S2). A large bunker lies between the driving area and the green (S4). Women's handicap 12 (S1).

penalty_areas: Tee shot carries over water.
green_features: Large bunker left, small bunker front-right, grass bunkers right and behind.
notes: Dogleg right; fairway bunker down the right (S4). In 2016 the rough right of the fairway bunker was replaced with trees and natural areas (S18). Women's handicap 8 (S1).

penalty_areas: Water down the right side starting about 150 yards from the green, held by a bulkhead, and wrapping behind the green.
green_slope: Two tiers; slopes left to right toward the water.
green_features: Spectator mound behind the green.
notes: Reachable par 5 (S4) and the easiest hole at the 2025 PLAYERS (S2); oak trees block the left (S4). New tee in 2025 (523 to 537 yards) (S13). Women's handicap 4 (S1).

penalty_areas: Island green: water surrounds the green on every side except the walkway (about 4 ft deep).
green_features: 3,912 sq ft, 78 ft deep x 81 ft wide (Golf News Net). Wide green that narrows to the right; one small pot bunker, placed on the right by the official hole guide (S4). In 2016 the collar was narrowed, which enlarged the putting surface. Contours were softened in 2007.
notes: Often called the Island Green (a nickname, not an official hole name). A drop area sits about 75 yards from the centre of the green (S9). The walkway is in play (S8). Women's handicap 16 (S1).

penalty_areas: Lake along the entire left side; the same lake borders the right of No. 9.
green_features: Grass bunkers front-right; one bunker left and long; spectator mound behind the green.
notes: Dogleg left; spectator mounds and trees right (S4). Second-hardest hole at the 2025 PLAYERS (S2). Women's handicap 6 (S1).

name: Outward Bound
green_features: Two-tier green ringed by deep bunkers (S3).
notes: Bunkers and dunes left of the landing area and thick rough right (S3); a slight dogleg left (S4).

name: Cross Country
green_features: A deep pot bunker short of a narrow green that runs off steeply to the right (S3, S4).
notes: Favour the left off the tee, which leaves a blind second shot (S3, S4).

name: O'Man
penalty_areas: Lake Michigan left (S3, S4).
green_features: A huge, undulating green with many pin positions (S3, S4).
notes: Lake Michigan, deep bunkers and dunes all down the left (S3, S4).

name: Glory
penalty_areas: Lake Michigan beyond the dunes on the left (S3, S4).
green_features: An elevated, well-guarded green on the bluff (S3, S4).
notes: The fairway tilts left toward bunkers, dunes and the lake, with mounds on the right (S3, S4).

name: Snake
penalty_areas: Water on both sides of the fairway and short and left of the green (S3, S4).
green_features: A shallow green with water short and left (S3).
notes: A narrow fairway with water on both sides that turns sharply right; going for the green in two needs a long carry (S3, S4).

name: Gremlin's Ear
green_features: A small, shallow green with a deep pot bunker in front (S3, S4).
notes: A short dogleg right, the shortest par 4 on the front nine (S3, S4).

name: Shipwreck
penalty_areas: Lake Michigan right (S3, S4).
green_features: A long, angled green surrounded by deep bunkers (S3, S4).
notes: Lake Michigan along the right; bunkers and a hill on the left (S3, S4).

name: On the Rocks
penalty_areas: Lake Michigan below the dunes on the right (S3, S4).
green_features: A long green falling away steeply to the lake on the right (S3).
notes: A blind tee shot with trouble on the right, where the ground drops toward the dunes and the lake (S3, S4).

name: Down and Dirty
penalty_areas: Seven Mile Creek by the green (S3, S4).
green_features: A two-tier, humpback green guarded by Seven Mile Creek and bunkers (S3, S4).
notes: The fairway tilts right; a large tree about 100 yards short of the green (S3).

name: Voyageur
green_features: An elevated green with subtle, hard-to-read breaks (S3, S4).
notes: A deep bunker about 240 yards off the tee (S3); it sits on the right (S4).

name: Sand Box
green_features: A small, elevated green; the approach can be blind (S3, S4).
notes: Dunes, bunkers and a drop-off down the right; a deep bunker about 100 yards short of the green (S3, S4).

name: Pop Up
penalty_areas: Lake Michigan below the bluff on the right (S3, S4).
green_features: A large, undulating green; deep bunkers long and a 40 ft drop toward Lake Michigan on the right (S3).
notes: A downhill par 3, the shortest hole on the course (S3, S4).

name: Cliff Hanger
penalty_areas: Lake Michigan below the bluffs on the right (S3, S4).
green_features: A narrow green on the bluffs (S4).
notes: Dunes and rough on the right, where the bluffs above the lake take anything that strays (S3, S4).

name: Widow's Watch
green_features: A heavily guarded green: trouble left and long (S3), deep bunkers on the right (S4).
notes: Thick rough right; an approach from the left is blind (S3). A long iron off the tee favours the right (S4).

name: Grand Strand
green_features: A huge green (S3).
notes: A long par 4 with deep dunes on the right (S3, S4); the approach carries dunes (S3, S4).

name: Endless Bite
penalty_areas: Lake Michigan beyond the green (S3, S4).
green_features: An elevated green approached uphill over dunes, with the lake behind it (S3, S4).
notes: The shortest par 5: the tee shot carries dunes (S4) and the green is reachable in two (S3).

name: Pinched Nerve
penalty_areas: Lake Michigan beyond the dunes on the left (S3).
green_features: Bunkers below the green on the left; misses right find dunes (S3, S4).
notes: Dunes and bunkers well below the green on the left, with a drop toward Lake Michigan; bunkers and a steep hill on the right (S3, S4).

name: Dyeabolical
penalty_areas: Seven Mile Creek in front of the green (S3, S4).
green_features: Seven Mile Creek guards the front of the green (S3, S4).
notes: An aggressive line carries about 300 yards of dunes on the left (S3, S4); Seven Mile Creek guards the tee shot and the approach (S4).

penalty_areas: No water or other penalty area is described on this hole by the club or the 2026 KPMG guide.
green_slope: Back-right to front-left, with a narrow opening at the front left (S6).
green_features: Three tiers; bunkered on every side except long (S9); three greenside bunkers (S6). Hitting the right tier is the key (S5, S11).
notes: Fairway bunkers on both sides squeeze the landing area (three of them, S6); they were moved closer to the fairway for 2009 (S16). 2016 Ryder Cup: played 442 because a grandstand blocked the 490 championship tee (S6, S12). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 490 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 442, played as Ryder Cup No. 1 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 439 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 417 (S9). Women's handicap 7 (S2).

penalty_areas: No water or other penalty area is described on this hole by the club or the 2026 KPMG guide.
green_features: Large bunkers guard the front left (S5, S9, S11); four greenside bunkers and subtle breaks (S6); deep bunkers left (S15).
notes: Dogleg left. For 2009 the left fairway bunker was moved so it is harder to carry, pushing play right toward two more bunkers (S16). Three fairway bunkers (S6). Hills were cut down in the 1970s so the fairway can be seen from the tee (S18). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 431 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 429, played as Ryder Cup No. 2 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 427 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 384 (S9). Women's handicap 9 (S2).

penalty_areas: No water or other penalty area is described on this hole by the club or the 2026 KPMG guide.
green_features: Large green with many demanding hole locations (S5, S9). One of the largest, deepest bunkers on the course guards all but the front left (S6).
notes: Two large bunkers left and thick rough right off the tee; a flat layup area about 130 yd short sets up a wedge (S9, S11). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 633 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 633, played as Ryder Cup No. 3 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 633 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 568 (S9). Women's handicap 15 (S2).

penalty_areas: No water: the only par 3 at Hazeltine without water (S6).
green_slope: Severe front-to-back slope; sidehill and downhill putts are hard (S11, S6).
green_features: Large two-tier green: a difficult back shelf about 10 yd deep and a flatter front, separated by a pronounced slope; small front-right section; bunkers all around (S9, S5). Only the back shelf's depth is published, not the whole green.
notes: Green speed and hole location are its main defence (S6). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 210 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 210, played as Ryder Cup No. 4 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 207 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 165 (S9). Women's handicap 11 (S2).

penalty_areas: No water or other penalty area is described on this hole by the club or the 2026 KPMG guide.
green_features: Narrow green, only a few paces wide at the opening, guarded by deep bunkers in front and on both sides (S5, S9, S6).
notes: Slight dogleg right with mature trees on the right and three fairway bunkers (S9, S6). Extended almost 50 yd for 2009 (Golf Channel says to 455; the card shows 448), with the right-side bunkers rebuilt closer to the fairway (S16). The No. 1 men's handicap hole (S1, S2). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 448 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 448, played as Ryder Cup No. 14 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 445 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 402 (S9). Women's handicap 1 (S2).

penalty_areas: Pond front and left of the green (S5, S6, S15); Golf Digest lists the 6th as one of three holes whose greens are guarded by ponds (S14).
green_features: Long, narrow green between bunkers on the right and the pond on the left (S5, S9, S11).
notes: Narrow fairway lined by trees on both sides (S5). Largely unchanged from the original layout (S5). Potentially drivable from forward tees (S6). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 405 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 405, played as Ryder Cup No. 15 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 406 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 380 (S9). Women's handicap 17 (S2).

penalty_areas: Large pond left of the green; water starts about 40 yd short and runs along the left to the back of the green (S9, S31, S5).
green_features: Hard to hold, especially downwind (S5, S9). The back-left corner appears to break uphill (S17).
notes: Shortest par 5; dogleg right and reachable in two (S6, S31). For 2009 a new tee at a different angle added 27 yd (S16). A new fairway built in 1977 removed a 90-degree dogleg right (S18). Fairway bunkers were added on the left of the landing area (S11). It was the easiest hole at the 2002 and 2009 PGA Championships (S31). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 572 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 572, played as Ryder Cup No. 16 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 568 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 516 (S9). Women's handicap 3 (S2).

penalty_areas: Pond in front of and right of the green; the club says the small green is encircled by water and sand (S5, S9, S11, S6). For championships the lateral relief option is removed, so a ball short in the water means dropping behind it and playing a third from about 100 yd (S7).
green_features: Long, small green with sand left (S9) and bunkers behind (S11); the narrow front section makes front hole locations dangerous (S11, S15).
notes: Justin Leonard (2002) and Padraig Harrington (2009) both lost a share of the PGA lead here (S7). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 176 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 176, played as Ryder Cup No. 17 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 173 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 152 (S9). Women's handicap 13 (S2).

penalty_areas: No water or other penalty area is described on this hole by the club or the 2026 KPMG guide.
green_features: Partly hidden from the fairway; sand short-left and along the right (S9); bunkers on both sides (S6); a depression on the right side (S13).
notes: Three bunkers on each side of the fairway (S9). In the 1970s it was rebuilt as an uphill, straight hole in place of a sharp dogleg left (S18). Northwest winds make it play hard (S6). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 432 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 432, played as Ryder Cup No. 18 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 432 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 394 (S9). Women's handicap 5 (S2).

penalty_areas: Hazeltine Lake left of and behind the green; back-left hole locations bring it into play, and an approach without spin can roll through into it (S5, S6, S32, S9).
green_slope: Front-right to back-left, falling sharply toward the lake (S6, S27).
green_features: A ridge divides the green, so two-putts from the wrong side are hard (S5, S9, S11). Bunkers short and right (S32).
notes: Dogleg left with three bunkers down the left (S32) and bunkers on both sides (S9); they were moved closer to the fairway for 2009 (S16). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 452 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 452, played as Ryder Cup No. 10 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 450 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 412 (S9). Women's handicap 8 (S2).

penalty_areas: No water is described on this hole by the club or the 2026 KPMG guide. Hazeltine Lake is in play on 10 and 16, not 11; no source puts it on this hole.
green_features: Large, strongly sloped green (S6); sand on the right of the approach (S9); a bunker about 30 yd short of the green was added for 2009 (S15).
notes: Double dogleg right with an hourglass fairway and 14 bunkers, tied for the most on the course (S6). A cluster of bunkers sits at the corner, and a big drive lets players go for the green in two (S11). Tournament setups: 2009 PGA Championship 606 (S15); 2016 Ryder Cup 606, played as Ryder Cup No. 11 (S12, S6); 2024 U.S. Amateur 606 (S19); 2026 KPMG Women's PGA 555 (S9). Women's handicap 14 (S2).

penalty_areas: No water or other penalty area is described on this hole by the club or the 2026 KPMG guide.

penalty_areas: Hazeltine Lake runs down the right, and the tee shot must carry it: 200+ yd from the championship tee (S6), about 220 yd (S15), and 150-200 yd from the members' back tees after the tee rebuild (S8). A creek runs down the left of the fairway (S5, S9). The peninsula green is surrounded by the lake, and hole locations on the right bring it into play (S9, S5).
green_features: Narrow, elevated peninsula green that angles away and is hard to hold (S5, S9, S11). It is the only hole on the course without a bunker (S24, S17).
notes: Signature hole; carts are not allowed on its fairway (S35). It was a 214-220 yd par 3 until it was converted to a par 4 after the 1970 U.S. Open; the old green was bulldozed into the lake to form the peninsula, and the new hole was first played publicly at the 1983 U.S. Senior Open (S8, S18, S19). It was lengthened 18 yd after 1991 (S8). Rees Jones later moved the tees back and up (S8: page dated 2025, section headed '2021 Changes'; S22 lists 2021 course updates). It played 396 yd at the 1991 U.S. Open (S7) and was the hardest hole at the 2002 PGA (S7). Wind off the lake is a major factor (S6, S27).
